notes.americas-1492: The denominator for the largest demographic catastrophe of the early modern world; it also sets the stakes for Indigenous environmental impact and the Anthropocene debate.
notes.justinianic-plague: Decides whether a pandemic belongs in the causal story of the end of antiquity and the Arab conquests, and whether plague can carry explanatory weight generally.
notes.quran-standardization: Fixes how far the text can be used as evidence for the first decades of Islam and for the religious authority of the early caliphate.
notes.khipu: A positive answer would give the Inka a readable documentary record and add a non-graphic system to the comparative history of writing.
notes.indus: Either outcome matters: a literate Harappa, or the main example of a large urban society run without writing.
notes.cocoliztli: Pathogen identity changes whether the Mexican collapse is framed as an inevitable consequence of contact or a product of colonial labour and famine.
notes.silver-china: Underpins the global-trade-after-1571 thesis and the silver-contraction explanation of the Ming fall.
notes.black-death-africa: Would overturn the assumption that sub-Saharan Africa was untouched by the second pandemic and reframe the background to the Atlantic encounter.
notes.copernicus-maragha: Whether the Copernican revolution is the end of an Islamic reform tradition or a Latin new start is a question about the shape of the history of science, not one subfield.
notes.roman-census: Nearly every account of Roman Italy, from the Gracchan crisis to slavery and recruitment, builds on one of the readings.
notes.plague-disappearance: Bears on whether early modern states could control epidemics by policy and on the origins of the eighteenth-century population rise.
notes.rongorongo: A pre-contact script would add a case to the handful of independent inventions of writing, from a society without cities or bureaucracy.
notes.meroitic: Would give Kush a history in its own voice rather than through Greek, Latin and Egyptian sources.
notes.gunpowder: The route matters for Mongol and Islamic intermediary debates, but gunpowder's arrival and effects are not in doubt.
notes.kerala-jesuits: A positive find would rewrite the origins of calculus; the more likely negative result changes little.
notes.shapira-scrolls: Genuine fragments would be the oldest biblical manuscript and bear on the Pentateuch's composition; a confirmed forgery is mainly a case study in authentication.
notes.mesopotamian-chronology: Shifts every pre-1400 BCE date in the Near East by up to 150 years, but mostly re-dates rather than re-interprets.
notes.zhou-conquest: A precise year would tidy Western Zhou chronology without changing how the period is understood.
notes.mendel: Important for how the episode is taught, but genetics and its history do not turn on whether the counts were tidied.
notes.vermeer: Settles a long argument about one painter's method and the Hockney-Falco thesis; limited reach beyond art history.
notes.wilkinson-ciphers: Would add detail to a well-established story of Spanish-American frontier intrigue.
notes.irish-1641: A defensible count matters for Irish historiography and memory, but the broad outline of the rising is not in question.
